shots.focal_element: The version tree list in the Add, Edit, or Delete Version screen, with the cursor on Working Budget
shots.typography: Native app UI text: small regular sans-serif in sentence/title case, normal tracking; white title on a solid blue header bar; bold for the selected row. No added motion-graphics type.
shots.what_happens: Full browser-window screen recording framed as a floating card with soft shadow over a white background and a large blue arc at the bottom. The cursor moves down the version tree to Working Budget while the narrator says they will copy the working budget (w195-w202); at the end a copy action opens a blank version form on the right.
shots.build_rebuild: Place a screen-recording video inside a rounded, drop-shadowed card at about 80% of frame width, centred on a white background with a large blue circular arc rising from the bottom edge.

shots.focal_element: The Name field in the Version Details panel as 'May Fo...' is typed
shots.typography: Native app UI labels in small regular sans-serif, title/sentence case, right-aligned field labels; typed value in the same UI face. No overlay type.
shots.what_happens: The camera pushes in from the full window toward the right-hand Version Details form and drifts right, while the version name 'May Forecast' is typed into the Name field in sync with 'call this new version the May forecast' (w204-w209).
shots.build_rebuild: Animate the recording card's scale from 1.0 to about 1.6 with an ease-in-out over roughly 0.5 s, anchored on the Name input, so the typing becomes legible.

shots.focal_element: The Start of plan field and its date-picker popup showing 5/1/2021, then the New Version Options checkboxes
shots.transition_other: Continuous camera move: the zoomed-in frame keeps panning down the form, with no visible cut
shots.typography: Native app UI text in small regular sans-serif; dropdown values and table headers in the same face, the selected row highlighted in light blue. Text is only legible because of the zoom.
shots.what_happens: While zoomed in, the camera tilts down to the Options group; the user opens the Start of plan picker, searches 5/1/2021 and selects it as the narration says actuals run through April and changes start in May (w210-w233). The view scrolls further to the New Version Options checklist, where a box is ticked, then pulls back out to the full window.
shots.build_rebuild: Keyframe the card's transform (translateY then scale back to 1.0) to follow the cursor down the form, holding on the date picker for about 3 s before an ease-in-out pull-out to the full-window framing.

shots.focal_element: A small 'Please wait...' progress dialog in the centre of the dimmed app window
shots.typography: Native modal text in small regular sans-serif, sentence case, dark on a light grey dialog.
shots.what_happens: After Save is clicked (w235-w237), the app dims behind a modal with a progress bar while the narration explains that the data and rules are being copied (w238-w245); in the last frame the dialog clears and the undimmed version list returns.
shots.build_rebuild: Show the full-window card with a 60% black overlay on the app area and a centred small dialog whose progress bar fills left to right over about 3 s, then cut the overlay away.

shots.focal_element: The new 'May Forecast' row highlighted in the version tree, with its Version Details on the right
on_screen_text: © 2020 Workday, Inc. All rights reserved. Proprietary and Confidential
shots.typography: Native app UI text in small regular sans-serif, title/sentence case; selected row highlighted in light blue; small grey footer legal text.
shots.what_happens: A long static hold on the full window showing the saved May Forecast version selected, while the narrator says the data has been copied and 'It's that quick and easy' (w246-w259). Near the end the app's blue left navigation menu slides open over a dimmed page and a submenu list appears, setting up 'review the results using the P&L sheet' (w260-w266).
shots.build_rebuild: Hold the full-window card for about 6 s, then slide in a solid blue left nav panel at about 15% of window width with a dark overlay over the rest, followed by a white submenu column.
